test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a primary difference between a primary and a secondary electrochemical cell?

options.text: A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged.
A secondary cell produces more energy than a primary cell.
A primary cell can be recharged, while a secondary cell cannot be recharged.
There is no difference between primary and secondary cells

solution:
The correct answer is __A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Primary electrochemical cells__ are designed for single-use and cannot be recharged.
 
• Examples of primary cells include alkaline batteries and zinc-carbon batteries.
 
• __Secondary electrochemical cells__ are rechargeable and can be reused multiple times.
 
• Examples of secondary cells include lithium-ion batteries and lead-acid batteries.
 
• The main difference lies in the reversibility of their chemical reactions during discharge and recharge.
 
• Secondary cells are more cost-effective over time due to their rechargeable nature.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Primary Cells:**

 
 
• Alkaline batteries are commonly used in remote controls and flashlights.
 
• Zinc-carbon batteries are used in clocks, toys, and radios.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Secondary Cells:**
 
 
• Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in smartphones, laptops, and electric vehicles.
 
• Lead-acid batteries are primarily used in automobiles and backup power systems.
 
 
 
• **Advantage of Secondary Cells:**
 
 
• They offer a sustainable and environmentally friendly solution for energy storage.
